A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same perturbed-cosine-router MoE study. Their text, equations, five tables, two figures and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison despite reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic experiments, language-modeling results and domain-generalization evaluations in Section 5, plus misspecified-model experiments in Appendix F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their outcomes in Section 5 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: The cosine and perturbed cosine routing formulas, norm perturbations and least-squares objectives remain unchanged. The added expert-network descriptions document existing experiments without establishing an architectural or procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic settings, Enwik8, Text8, Wikitext-103, and five DomainBed datasets: PACS, VLCS, OfficeHome, TerraIncognita and DomainNet. Appendix F retains the same misspecified data-generating scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments: vanilla cosine routing in the language-modeling and synthetic comparisons, and linear routing in domain generalization and Appendix F.2.

E3.justification: The stated synthetic settings, model sizes, routing configurations, metrics, training budgets and validation procedures are retained. Newly specified expert-layer and dropout details supplement documentation rather than revise previously stated settings.

E4.justification: Appendix F retains the same comparisons on linear-router-generated data using ReLU or quadratic experts. The domain-shift evaluations are also unchanged; no new ablation, sensitivity analysis or robustness experiment appears.

E5.justification: Both versions report 20 experiments per synthetic sample size, two-standard-deviation error bars, and averages over three runs for language modeling and domain generalization. No additional uncertainty-reporting procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 and Figures 1–2 retain their numerical results and trends. For example, average domain-generalization accuracies remain 65.40, 66.70 and 68.37 for linear, cosine and perturbed cosine routing, respectively; Appendix F's fitted convergence exponents also match.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 replaces L2-norm approximation and covering estimates with supremum-norm bounds in the proof of Theorem 1. Section 2 adds router-rate reasoning and a quadratic-expert calculation. The numbered theorem statements and identifiability assumptions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: potentially non-polynomial estimation under cosine routing and polynomial rates for identifiable experts under perturbed routing. The proposed contribution and headline scope remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 2 qualifies the parameter-rate interpretation to 'at least one' slow rate and makes expert slowdown conditional on the expert parameter's rate. It adds possible effects of slow routing on joint training and asserts Top-K applicability. Section 4 newly identifies unresolved approximation theory as an obstacle to misspecified-model analysis.

D1.justification: Appendices E.2–E.3 newly describe two-layer experts, ReLU/GELU activations, dropout of 0.1, and the domain-generalization hidden width of four times the input dimension. A new reproducibility statement promises code release upon acceptance; it does not supply released code.

R1.justification: v3 adds selected references concerning softmax properties, polynomial experts, Top-K routing, continual learning and minimax estimation, while removing GLaM and GShard references. These extend supporting context without substantially changing the paper's positioning relative to linear and cosine routing.

P1.justification: Localized theoretical discussion and implementation explanations are expanded. Acknowledgements and a reproducibility statement are added, references move before the appendices, citations switch to author–year style, and author/affiliation text changes. The scientific section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The document is extensively reset in the ICLR template, changing typography, margins, spacing and running headers. Tables become more compact, Tables 3–5 are grouped together, and Figure 2 occupies a separate final page. Existing displays are retained; Table 1's caption newly specifies 'worst possible' rates.

improvement.justification: The supremum-norm revision in Appendix B.1, more qualified Theorem 2 discussion and added expert-network details provide a limited gain in mathematical precision and reproducibility. These benefits outweigh a localized algebraic slip in the new quadratic-expert example, which prints |x| instead of |x|^2. The broader headline claims remain unchanged.
